title: Git in a Team: Pull Requests, Reviews and Merge Strategies
oneLiner: Remotes, pull requests, code review, merge versus squash versus rebase, and what to do when your push is rejected.
keyTakeaway: Branch from the latest main, keep pull requests small, let CI and a reviewer approve them, then merge with the team's strategy: a merge commit keeps everything, squash gives one commit per pull request, rebase gives a straight line with rewritten commits. Integrate others' work with pull --rebase; never force-push shared branches.
explanation:
Git Basics and Git Branching cover Git on your own machine. This lesson is about using it with other people: remotes, fetch versus pull, the life of a pull request, reviewing, branch protection, branching models and keeping secrets out of the history.

All terminal output in this lesson comes from real git 2.43 runs, including the three merge strategies applied to the same branch and a push rejected because a teammate pushed first.
